extracted.intended_audience: general readers, television viewers, and anyone researching the Carpool Karaoke segment or its adaptations
extracted.subtask_description: Document the defining features, production practices, distribution, and international adaptations of the 'Carpool Karaoke' television segment and its Apple Music series spin-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core segment format
rubrics_metrics.description: A recurring segment in which host James Corden invites famous musical guests to sing along to their songs with him while traveling in a car driven by Corden on a planned route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often performed as an informal sing-along in a moving vehicle; the segment's entertainment value rests on famous people singing in an ordinary situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretend premise / narrative framing
rubrics_metrics.description: The trip is usually under the pretense of needing to get to work and preferring to use the high-occupancy carpool vehicle lane, or the pretext of needing directions from a local when in a new town.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given include driving in Los Angeles using the carpool lane or needing directions in cities such as London (Adele), Liverpool (Paul McCartney), New York City (Madonna) or Las Vegas (Celine Dion). The premise supplies a casual, relatable framing for the segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned route and location
rubrics_metrics.description: Segments are filmed along a planned route, usually in Los Angeles, though episodes have been filmed in other cities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locations can be integral to the episode (e.g., London for Adele) and may affect guest selection, song choices, and staging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests are primarily famous musical artists, though occasionally non-musicians/high-profile public figures appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists many musical guests (e.g., Adele, Paul McCartney, Justin Bieber, Lady Gaga) and notes high-profile non-musician appearances (e.g., Michelle Obama). Guest stature contributes to viral potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Song selection and segment structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each segment typically features the guest performing or singing multiple songs (often hits) during the car trip; episode listings show multiple songs per appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episode lists show that segments commonly include medleys or several full songs — song choice, order, and variety affect pacing and viewer engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and production practice (driving vs towing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although presented as Corden driving the car, production sometimes tows the vehicle for safety, choreography, or costume changes; Corden does not always actually drive during filming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes towing was used in roughly five percent of the series to date, with specific examples (Meghan Trainor, Migos, Cardi B, Chance the Rapper, Justin Bieber). This is a production concession balancing realism and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and spin-off series model
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple Music and CBS Television Studios reached a deal for an exclusive first-window licensing agreement: Apple Music is the global home of a television series adaptation of the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series premiered August 8, 2017 on Apple Music; initial announcements suggested a single host would appear in every episode, but later reports indicated the series would use a different host in every episode. Season renewals and premiere dates are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viral/online performance as a success metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Segments are judged in part by their popularity on YouTube and online platforms; view counts are highlighted (e.g., Adele amassed 42 million views in five days and 233 million by March 12, 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists other segments that surpassed 100 million views and notes the most-viewed non-musician segment (Michelle Obama) as an indicator of reach and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primetime special and awards recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS aired a primetime special featuring highlights of the segment; the special won a 2016 Emmy Award for Outstanding Variety Special.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primetime specials and awards are described as markers of mainstream recognition and success beyond the late-night slot.

rubrics_metrics.name: International adaptations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Carpool Karaoke format has been adapted internationally, with country-specific versions that include local hosts and networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article provides a table of international versions (Algeria, France, Israel, Italy, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Slovenia, UAE, etc.), showing that the format is transferable but localized with different hosts and premiere dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode documentation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Episodes are documented with episode number, guest(s), date of first broadcast, and songs performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structured listing demonstrates an archival standard for tracking segments and provides an implicit criterion for completeness when documenting or producing episodes.
